subject: Operational deep-dive: infra + model-serving 60-90m slot
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Kaitlyn Price <kaitlyn@avasystems.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Operational deep-dive: infra + model-serving 60-90m slot

Hi Kaitlyn — great speaking earlier. Quick recap and proposed next step so we can bring engineering and infra folks into the conversation:

Recap (from our call)
- Primary goal: reduce tail latency for inference and get predictable per-call cost for customer-facing autopilot features.
- Key constraints: HIPAA-adjacent data flows, want optional VPC/private deployment, KMS integration, and audit logs.
- Current models: mix of open and in-house fine-tuned LLMs; interested in quantization/throughput tradeoffs.

Recommended next step
- 60–90 minute technical deep-dive (TDX) with Redwood ML + Infra (we cover serving runtime, batching/caching, quantization profile choices, routing/fallbacks, and security/KMS patterns).
- Goal: emerge with a mutual action plan (objectives, success metrics, attendees, and a target pilot timeframe).

Can you share 2–3 windows that work for your engineers next week? Suggested attendee roles from your side: engineering manager, infra/ops lead, and security/contact for KMS questions. From our side I’ll bring Connor (serving runtime), Marcus (infra & deployment), and Marissa for success metrics & rollout plan.

I attached a short prep checklist and a sample ops runbook so folks can skim ahead of time (tdx-prep-checklist.pdf, sample-ops-runbook.md).

Proposed agenda (we can compress/expand):
- 0–10m: objectives & current architecture recap (you)
- 10–35m: serving runtime deep-dive — batching, KV cache, latency SLOs (Connor)
- 35–55m: deployment patterns — Dedicated vs Private, autoscaling & cost levers (Marcus)
- 55–70m: security & compliance / KMS integration (Marissa + open Q&A)
- 70–90m: next steps / mutual action plan

Thanks, and happy to coordinate calendar invites once you confirm availability.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

Attachments: tdx-prep-checklist.pdf (5 pages), sample-ops-runbook.md (code + notes)

Connor / Marcus — Kaitlyn at Ava Systems proposed two windows (they'll confirm one): Tue 15 Jun 10:00–11:30 PT or Wed 16 Jun 13:00–14:30 PT. Confirm availability? If you can only do one of those, call it out and I’ll push for the other.

Requested prep from each of you (short bullets to present):
- Connor: 10–20 slides showing batching behavior at different qps, KV cache warmup profile, and an example of prefix caching to reduce per-call tokens. Include p50/p95/p99 numbers if you have recent test runs.
- Marcus: deployment options summary (Dedicated vs Private), autoscaling policy examples, and expected cost ranges for the two patterns (ballpark $/k-token).
- Marissa: quick note on rollout and monitoring (SLOs to track, regression detection, and a sample alerting threshold).

Kaitlyn also asked specifically about p99 benchmarks for Dedicated vs Private and KV cache warmup — Connor, if you can paste a short benchmark snippet (p50/p95/p99) into a reply here, I’ll pass it along to them pre-meeting.

I’ll draft the calendar invite once we lock a time and will attach the same prep materials we shared earlier.

Thanks — Soojin

Confirmed attendees (Ava Systems): Kaitlyn Price (Product), Tom Ruiz (Engineering Manager), Priya Shah (Security).

- 30–50m: deployment patterns & autoscaling policy (Marcus)

Kaitlyn — attached again is the prep checklist and a short runbook; Connor also pasted a quick benchmark snippet below as requested:

--- benchmark snippet (Connor) ---
p50/p95/p99 (synthetic, inference-only)
- Dedicated (g5-like): 18ms / 34ms / 78ms
- Private (m40-quantized path): 22ms / 46ms / 120ms

If anything else comes up before the call, reply-all and we’ll adjust. Looking forward to it.
